newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Tabcorp says Sky sets deadline.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Tabcorp says Sky sets deadline.

text.p: Wagering and gaming group Tabcorp Holdings Ltd said on Friday that Sky Channel would cease supply of televised racing to it on October 1 unless Tabcorp accepted a 164 percent price increase for the service.
"We are very disappointed that Sky will not renegotiate and are not prepared to reduce the fee demanded in any way," Tabcorp managing director Ross Wilson said in a statement.
Sky had rejected an earlier counter-offer by Tabcorp to pay a 150 percent fee increase, he said.

Under a contract that ran out in June, Tabcorp, which operates in Victoria only, was charged about A$3 million a year for the channel, passing on about half of that cost to its commissioned betting agencies, or TABs.

Sky, owned equally by businessman Kerry Packer's Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd and Rupert Murdoch's News Corp Ltd, holds a virtual monopoly on direct television broadcasts of greyhound, thoroughbred and harness racing in Australia.
Sky managing director Bill North earlier told Reuters that the price increase was intended to recoup the cost of securing sole broadcasting rights for Victorian content.
The Victorian agencies' association has said the channel was vital to attracting punters and more than half of the TAB's in the state would have to close if they lost the broadcasts.

Tabcorp has declined to comment on possible closures but said in its statement that it would try to minimise the effect on the company on losing Sky by transferring business to its other betting outlets, including clubs, hotels and racecourses.
In the year to June 30, 1996 Tabcorp's net profit was A$63.4 million on turnover of A$557 million, 48 percent of which came from TAB agencies.
Tabcorp shares closed four cents up at A$6.25.
